title: Warmup runs — applied-ml standup notes (Jun 03 2026)
content:
Standup: Warmup runs / micro-eval pipeline kick — notes + action items

Attendees: Maya (owner), Arjun, Sophie, Ibrahim, Dan (brief join)
Date: 2026-06-03
Location: Zoom / #applied-ml

Goal for this week:
- Get deterministic warmup runs for the compact-model onboarding flow so that nightly micro-evals are stable across infra restarts.
- Validate 4-bit quantized checkpoint (kv-friendly) on 512-token convs with microbatch=8.
- Surface simple regression checks for hallucination rate on the NQ-style eval slice.

Quick summary of experiments run overnight:
1) run: warmup/kv-prefetch/seed-20260602-a
   - model: compact-3B-4bit-kv (int4 asymmetric per-channel)
   - infra: dev-gpu-pool-12 (A100-sim), microbatch=8, prefix-cache enabled
   - result: throughput 210 tokens/s, median latency 62ms/token during tails
   - note: observed KV-prefetch misses for very short prompts (<16 tokens) due to key alignment offset in loader; likely off-by-one in prefetch window config.

2) run: micro-eval/nq-hallucination-probe-512
   - dataset: 1200 NQ-derived examples (reduced context ambiguity)
   - metric: Factuality-precision @ top1 (heuristic: answer match + support sentence overlap)
   - baseline (fp16): precision 0.88
   - compact-4bit: precision 0.81 (delta -0.07)
   - initial calibration: applying 16-bit softmax temp adjust recovered +0.02 precision but increased repetition on multi-turns.

Observations / hypotheses:
- The compact 4-bit path shows predictable drop in precision on edge questions with long context dependencies (supports hypothesis that KV quantization noise accumulates across layers).
- The KV-prefetch miss pattern explains some of the latency spikes; misaligned prefetch reduces effective cache hit ratio from ~0.68 --> ~0.53 on short prompts.
- Microbatch=8 seems acceptable for throughput target but increases p99 latency variance when a single request has long generation (>400 tokens). Consider adaptive microbatching.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Stop-gap: add a configuration knob to extend prefetch window by +1 key for short prompts. Arjun to push patch. (Jira RED-3412)
- Evals: add a small NQ-focused regression test to nightly micro-eval that flags precision drop > 0.04 vs baseline. Sophie will author the test harness.
- Onboarding checklist: require at least two warmup runs with consistent token-level latency profiles before marking a model onboarding PR as "ready-for-dedicated". Ibrahim owner for checklist updates.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Arjun Patel: implement prefetch-window-fix, run 3 replicates, attach logs to RED-3412. ETA: 2026-06-05.
- Sophie Laurent: write NQ precision smoke test, integrate into micro-eval pipeline, PR #87 review. ETA: 2026-06-07.
- Ibrahim Okafor: update onboarding runbook with warmup acceptance criteria and sample commands. ETA: 2026-06-06.
- Maya Chen: run longer tails experiment (1000 examples, max gen 1024) to observe p99 behavior and KV accumulation effect; record sample failures. ETA: 2026-06-08.

Unresolved questions / open investigations:
- Is the drop in factuality primarily due to per-channel quantization granularity or our fused-kernel numerics? Need a small ablation: run identical weights with fake-quant (simulate noise) vs real quant kernels. (Sophie/Arjun)
- Should we add a "quant-sensitivity" label in the model catalog metadata so downstream services can opt into higher-precision fallback for specific routes? (Product thought)
- Cost tradeoff: at scale, moving to microbatch=4 with slightly higher throughput per-GPU could reduce p99 variance but increase unit cost. Need quick cost sim. (Finance + Infra)

Commands / reproducibility notes (notes to self):
- warmup run command (dev cluster): ./scripts/warmup_run.sh --model compact-3B-4bit-kv --microbatch 8 --seed 20260602 --prefix-cache true --outdir /tmp/warmup-20260602-a
- micro-eval launcher: python tools/micro_eval.py --dataset data/nq_reduced.jsonl --model-path /tmp/warmup-20260602-a/checkpoint.pt --max-gen 512 --num-replicates 3 --save-preds preds.jsonl
- quick log grep pattern for prefetch-miss: grep -E "PREFETCH.*miss.*offset" /tmp/warmup-20260602-a/logs/* | head -n 50

Notes to reviewers / context: 
- This is intentionally a working note — contains raw experiment outputs and subjective heuristics. Please tag me in PRs or Slack threads. If you iterate on the prefetch window change, include a short perf leak check (compare median throughput across 20 short-run samples).

Lightweight retrospective: what went well
- Nightly micro-eval pipeline caught a repeatable regression instead of it surfacing in customer traffic. Good signal from the NQ slice.
- Small cross-functional alignment (SRE + infra) happened quickly because we had concrete logs.

What to improve next week:
- Better structured micro-eval reports (single-line summaries per model + clear pass/fail): Sophie to propose a template.
- Automate the alignment check for prefetch-window in the loader unit tests. Arjun to add test.

Copy of quick experiment table (raw numbers):
- compact-3B-fp16 | throughput 235 t/s | median token-lat 58ms | NQ-precision 0.88
- compact-3B-4bit-kv | throughput 210 t/s | median token-lat 62ms | NQ-precision 0.81
- compact-3B-4bit-kv + temp-adjust | throughput 206 t/s | median token-lat 63ms | NQ-precision 0.83

Attachments / places to look:
- RED-3412: prefetch window bug + logs
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/quant-playbook/pull/87 (Sophie)
- Confluence: compact-onboard-runbook (draft section: warmup acceptance)

End notes (stream-of-consciousness / to-self):
- If the ablation shows kernel numerics are the issue, schedule a deeper perf/accuracy trade study with research group.
- Consider a small on-device float reinstatement for top-L layers as a mitigation (costly but might recover factuality).

-- maya
